tier_reason: invoice-core is a library crate: Cargo.toml declares no [[bin]] and no [[example]], src/ contains no main(), and nothing in the repo opens a socket. There is no process to start and no URL to open, so renders is unreachable by construction rather than by a missing dependency. The crate compiles and its 7 unit tests run, which is build_and_test. This amendment adds a coverage report and does not change the tier.

commands.install: rustup component add clippy llvm-tools-preview && cargo fetch --locked && (command -v cargo-llvm-cov >/dev/null 2>&1 || cargo install cargo-llvm-cov --locked --version "^0.9")

env.name: RUST_BACKTRACE
env.why: The crate itself reads no environment variable anywhere (no env::var, env!, or option_env! in src/). This one is the test harness's own configuration, set to its real value so that when a verifier makes a change that panics, the test output names the frame instead of telling it to re-run with a backtrace it cannot then re-run with. Nothing in the library depends on it.

dropped.from: the amendment report coverage-and-checkers, static_checks half
dropped.what: A declared static check running clippy, e.g. cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --message-format=json | clippy-sarif > clippy.sarif
dropped.why: The factory already runs clippy itself, so this would be a second copy of the same checker rather than one the factory does not run. Measured here: bsf's native runner is `cargo clippy --quiet --message-format=json -- -W clippy::all` (runStaticTools pushes it for any repo with a Cargo.toml), and measuredCounts sums every tool's counts per rule per file. With one probe unwrap() in library code and one in a #[cfg(test)] module, the native command reported clippy::unwrap_used at src/money.rs:50 once; adding --all-targets reported line 50 twice, because the lib is compiled again as the unit-test target. Declaring it would therefore have counted a single library unwrap three times and listed every finding three times in the gate output. The test-module finding the native run misses (line 79) is already a hard failure in the repo's own ci.yml, which runs cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings on every pull request. Paying triple-counted, triple-listed findings for coverage the repo's CI already enforces is a worse gate, so static_checks is left empty on purpose rather than by omission. clippy is the only checker this repo uses: ci.yml runs nothing else, and there is no rustfmt.toml, no .gitleaks.toml, no cargo-deny and no cargo-audit.

It is a lint, not a build. `bsf gates static` runs clippy itself through its own rule pack and compares each rule's count per file against .factory/guardrails/baselines.json, which is the point of Cargo.toml setting clippy::unwrap_used to "warn" rather than "deny". Putting -D warnings in the sandbox's build command would fail the build on the first new warning and hide the per-rule comparison the gate exists to make. The install command still adds the clippy component so the gate has it.
Release metadata. `cargo publish` is disabled in the manifest and nothing in the sandbox should attempt it; there is no packaging or release step to carry over.

dropped.what: The stated build commands were re-derived rather than copied
dropped.why: The README gives `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`. Both were run here before being recorded; `--all-targets` was added to the test command so that example and integration targets a builder adds later are compiled by the same command, matching ci.yml rather than the README's shorter form.

dropped.what: cargo llvm-cov --html / --cobertura / --json, and cargo llvm-cov report --open
dropped.why: The gate reads one file in one format. lcov is the format cargo-llvm-cov emits natively and one bsf's readCoverage parses directly, so no conversion step is needed; generating the others would add time to every pull request for output nothing reads.

dropped.what: Writing the report to coverage/lcov.info, which is also bsf's default discovery path
dropped.why: `.gitignore` ignores only /target and .playwright-cli/, so a coverage/ directory left behind by an agent that ran the command locally is untracked and lands in a diff the first time anything does `git add -A`. target/coverage/lcov.info is inside the already-ignored /target, and the path is declared in coverage_report so discovery is not relied on.

exercised: Compiling the crate and all its targets from source with cargo build --all-targets. After the install step nothing further is fetched, because the dependency and dev-dependency tables are both empty.

Running the 7 unit tests in src/money.rs and src/invoice.rs with cargo test --all-targets: amount parsing, rejection of non-money input, half-away-from-zero rounding in basis points, two-place formatting, line subtotals, tax taken on the net total rather than per line, and the empty invoice.

Measuring line coverage, new in this amendment. `mkdir -p target/coverage && cargo llvm-cov --all-targets --lcov --output-path target/coverage/lcov.info` runs the same 7 tests under instrumentation and writes lcov at target/coverage/lcov.info. Verified here from a removed target/ directory: exit 0, two SF records (src/invoice.rs LF:30 LH:30, src/money.rs LF:55 LH:55), so 85 of 85 lines, which bsf's fromLcov reads as 100%. This is what the tests gate runs in place of commands.test, so diff coverage of a changed file is now measurable instead of the coverage gate reporting that there is no report.

Failing the tests gate when a test fails, through the coverage command rather than only through cargo test. Verified by changing the expected net in adds_the_lines_and_the_tax: cargo llvm-cov exited 101 and printed "6 passed; 1 failed", so substituting it for commands.test does not silently turn a red test green.

Calling the library directly from a scratch example, which is how a verifier sees behaviour here since there is nothing to open or curl. Verified in setup: writing examples/scratch_check.rs against the names re-exported from lib.rs (Cents, Invoice, Line, Total) and running cargo run --example scratch_check printed net 64.97, tax 12.99, gross 77.96 for three lines of 19.99 plus one of 5.00 at 2000 bps, and None for the bad amount "1.5".

Linting with clippy: cargo clippy --all-targets runs clean, and the clippy component is installed by the install command so `bsf gates static` has the tool it needs for the clippy::unwrap_used baseline. Confirmed in this episode that the static gate does run clippy on this repo without anything being declared: runStaticTools adds it for any root holding a Cargo.toml.

Rebuilding offline after install: the empty [dependencies] and [dev-dependencies] tables mean the crate itself fetches nothing, so a change that adds a dependency is visible as the first command that needs the network.

not_exercised.what: Anything a browser, an HTTP client or a running process would show. There is no screenshot, no page and no endpoint.
not_exercised.why: The crate has no binary target and no server. This is the repo's stated purpose as a fixture: runtime verification where there is nothing to open and nothing to curl. A verifier has to call the code from a scratch example or a test, which is listed under exercised.

not_exercised.what: Lint coverage of code inside #[cfg(test)] modules, examples and benches, by the factory's static gate. The gate's own clippy run uses the default target set, so a warning that only appears when the test target is compiled is not counted and not baselined.
not_exercised.why: Measured, not assumed: a probe unwrap() inside src/money.rs's #[cfg(test)] mod tests was absent from the native command's output while the one in library code was reported. It is left uncovered by the factory because closing it means declaring a second clippy run, which triple-counts every library finding (see dropped). The repo's own ci.yml already fails the pull request on it with cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, so the warning is caught, just not by the factory's per-rule baseline.

not_exercised.what: Branch coverage. The lcov report carries BRF:0 and BRH:0 for both files, so only line coverage is real.
not_exercised.why: cargo-llvm-cov derives lcov from LLVM region counters and does not emit branch records. bsf's fromLcov reads only SF, LF, LH and end_of_record, so it measures lines and nothing in the gate asks for branches. A fully line-covered match arm with an untested branch would still read as covered.

not_exercised.what: Coverage figures that exclude test code. The 100% total counts the lines of the #[cfg(test)] mod tests blocks themselves, because they live in the same files as the code they test.
not_exercised.why: cargo-llvm-cov can exclude whole files with --ignore-filename-regex, and this repo has no tests/ directory to exclude: the tests are inside src/money.rs and src/invoice.rs. So the total is flattering by construction. Diff coverage, which is the check with teeth at diff_min_pct 80, is affected the same way: a change that adds a function and a test for it in the same file counts the test's own lines as covered.

not_exercised.what: Documentation tests. Neither cargo test --all-targets nor cargo llvm-cov --all-targets runs doctests, so they are absent from both the tests gate and the coverage report.
not_exercised.why: This matches ci.yml, which also uses --all-targets. The doc comments in all three files are prose explaining why a rule exists and contain no ``` examples, so there is nothing to run today. If a builder adds a doc example, cargo test --doc would be needed and is in neither command.

not_exercised.what: Integer overflow behaviour in release mode. Cents::basis_points computes self.0 * bps without checked arithmetic, unlike Cents::parse which uses checked_mul and checked_add.
not_exercised.why: Everything here runs on the dev profile, where arithmetic overflow panics; a release build wraps silently instead. Nothing in the sandbox builds or tests with --release, so the two profiles' behaviour for an extreme amount is not compared. Noted as an observation about what verification covers, not as a claim about whether the current behaviour is wrong.

There is none: no async runtime, no filesystem or database access, no HTTP client, and no third-party crate at all. The services and stubs lists are empty because the app genuinely needs neither, not because they could not be reached.

episode.tried: Amendment, from report coverage-and-checkers: "the coverage gate reports no coverage report on every PR, so diff coverage is never measured; and where the factory has no built-in checker for the language, the static gate checks nothing." Before changing anything, read how the runner actually consumes both halves: runTestsGate, gatesTests, gatesCoverage, runCoverageGate, readCoverage/fromLcov, runStaticTools, runClippy, runSarifCheck, countSarif and measuredCounts in bsf.mjs, plus .factory/definition/factory.yaml and the verification job in .github/workflows/factory-gates.yml.
episode.observed: Four facts decided the rest. (1) gatesTests runs `build && coverage` in place of the test command when commands.coverage is set, so the report is written by the tests gate; gatesCoverage does not run anything, it only reads the file. (2) Both run in the same verification job, after `bsf sandbox start`, which itself runs commands.install, so anything the coverage command needs has to be installed there. (3) closedEnv keeps PATH and HOME from the runner, so a cargo subcommand in ~/.cargo/bin is still reachable under the closed environment. (4) existing_ci.test_check is null in factory.yaml, so the tests gate really does run the command rather than reading ci.yml's result. Also noted the cost of declaring coverage_report: runCoverageGate turns a missing report from neutral into a failure.
episode.changed: Decided the shape before running anything: cargo-llvm-cov in install, the coverage command writing lcov, and coverage_report declared.

episode.tried: Settled the static_checks half empirically rather than by reading. Inserted two probe unwrap() calls into src/money.rs, one in library code and one inside the #[cfg(test)] mod tests, then ran bsf's exact native command, `cargo clippy --quiet --message-format=json -- -W clippy::all`, and the --all-targets --all-features form a declared check would use, parsing both JSON streams the same way runClippy does.
episode.observed: The native command reported clippy::unwrap_used at src/money.rs:50 once and did not report the test-module one at line 79 at all. The --all-targets form reported line 50 twice and line 79 once, because the lib is compiled a second time as the unit-test target. Since runStaticTools pushes native clippy for any repo with a Cargo.toml and measuredCounts sums counts per rule per file across tools, a declared clippy check would have made one library unwrap count three and appear three times in the findings list. ci.yml already runs cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings on every pull request, so the line-79 class of warning is a hard CI failure today.

The install took 63s from source. BRF and BRH are both 0: there are no branch records.
